person typing. A frame has to be recognisable in a stream that is mostly not
frames, and unrecognised bytes discardable without desynchronising the next.

A CHECKSUM because a truncated frame is plausible: a host that closes

kinds.name: request
kinds.doc: A client asking a world something.

kinds.name: response
kinds.doc: A world's answer, correlated by request_id.

kinds.name: log
kinds.doc: A LogLine, pushed to a subscriber.

kinds.name: heartbeat
kinds.doc: A periodic WorldState, so silence means something.

doc: FNV-1a, little-endian on the wire. Enough to catch truncation and
corruption, and not pretending to be more.
NEVER ZERO: that value means 'no checksum recorded' for a stored payload,
and a body whose real hash is zero would silently become unverified. The
control channel does not need that distinction but must not contradict it,
because both share one function.

limits.name: max_payload
doc: The largest payload a frame may carry. Bounded so a corrupt length cannot
make a world allocate against a number it read off a wire.

limits.name: max_request
doc: The largest app request a world accepts for pass-through. Bigger than any
widget can collect — a person types one field — and smaller than a frame,
because this bounds what is COPIED into a fixed slot while it waits.

limits.name: envelope_slack
doc: Room for the fields AROUND a payload: a verb, a correlation id, their
tags. Named rather than folded into the sums so it is obvious what the
spare bytes are for.

limits.name: max_log_line
limits.doc: The longest line the log will frame. Bounded by the panel and the report format.

limits.name: notice_slots
doc: How many framed notices a world keeps for a client that has not read them.
About four screens of bring-up; beyond that the oldest go and the count of
what went is reported rather than quietly dropped.

limits.name: max_refusal_text
doc: The longest sentence a stack-built refusal may carry. Everything needing
more than this needs a heap and can wait for one.

derived.name: frame_overhead
derived.doc: Everything a frame costs beyond its payload.

derived.name: inbound
doc: What a world holds while reassembling an inbound frame. A frame larger
than this can never complete, so a world REFUSES one that says it is —
rather than sliding bytes forever while the sender waits.

derived.name: notice_frame
derived.doc: One framed LogLine, and the slot that holds it.

derived.name: refusal_body
derived.doc: A ControlResponse carrying one sentence and a correlation id.

derived.name: refusal_frame
derived.doc: The same, framed — the answer a world can give before it has a heap.
